security_audit.summary: Static alerts were caused by Markdown code fences, inline component names, Python import examples, and a relative frontend fetch example. I found no evidence of prompt injection, hidden execution, credential access, external exfiltration, or malicious intent. The skill is instructional content, but authors should add explicit validation and authorization guidance around server-handled actions.

remediation.issue: Server action examples mutate data from action payloads without making authorization checks prominent.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit payload validation and user permission checks before form.submit, confirm.accept, and other data-changing actions.

remediation.issue: The entity search example interpolates the query directly into a relative URL.
remediation.suggestion: Show URLSearchParams or equivalent encoding and add guidance for query length limits and rate limiting.

content.value_statement: Interactive chat products need buttons, forms, entity mentions, and reliable action handling. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical widget patterns for client and server workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains client-handled and server-handled ChatKit widget actions.
Shows widget template patterns for lists, buttons, layouts, text, images, and icons.
Guides backend action handlers that replace widgets and emit client effects.
Covers entity tagging, search callbacks, and entity click navigation.
Documents common validation errors for payloads, contexts, and synthetic messages.
limitations: Focuses on ChatKit-style widgets, not every chat framework.
Does not provide a complete production application or deployment setup.
Example code needs project-specific authorization, validation, and tests.
Does not replace official API reference documentation.

use_cases.title: Design Clickable Chat Results
use_cases.description: Create list widgets with buttons and item selection for article, task, or product results.

use_cases.title: Handle Server Actions
use_cases.description: Implement backend handlers that process widget actions, update data, and replace widget state.

use_cases.title: Prototype Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Combine composer tools, entity mentions, and widgets to test guided AI workflows quickly.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Basic Widget
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple interactive chat widget for selecting one item from a list. Include the widget structure, action payload, and expected user flow.

prompt_templates.title: Add Client Actions
prompt_templates.prompt: Add client-handled actions to an existing chat widget. Include navigation, local state updates, and clear action names.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Server Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a server action handler for a form submission widget. Include payload validation, permission checks, widget replacement, and user feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Full Widget Lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a complete interactive chat workflow with entity tagging, composer modes, client actions, server actions, error states, and test cases.

output_examples.input: Create a widget that lets users choose an article and open details.
output_examples.output: A plan for a list widget with article rows, a client action for opening details, and payload fields for article identity.

output_examples.input: Add a server action for confirming a selected task.
output_examples.output: A backend flow that validates the task id, checks user permission, updates the task, replaces the widget, and sends confirmation feedback.

output_examples.input: Support mentions for people and documents in the chat composer.
output_examples.output: An entity tagging design with search behavior, grouped results, click handling, and backend conversion into model-readable context.

best_practices: Validate action payloads before navigation, database updates, or agent handoff.
Keep client and server action ownership clear for every action type.
Test widget rendering, payload handling, error states, and replacement events together.
anti_patterns: Handling the same widget action in both client and server code.
Copying examples without project-specific authorization checks.
Treating RequestContext as a plain dictionary instead of the provided object.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build interactive AI chat widgets with buttons, forms, entity mentions, and action handlers.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include server-side patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for server actions, widget replacement, synthetic messages, and client effects.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that developers adapt inside their own application.

faq.question: Is authentication handled for me?
faq.answer: No. You must add your own authentication, authorization, input validation, and audit logging.

faq.question: When should I not use this skill?
faq.answer: Do not use it for simple text-only chat where no interactive widget behavior is needed.
